assessment.summary: Sharing should become one authenticated, versioned vault state machine rather than a collection of independently patched file operations.

assumptions: No measured latency or memory budget was supplied.
Single-writer serialization is acceptable unless product requirements say otherwise.

opportunities.title: Make sharing an authenticated, versioned vault state machine
opportunities.summary: Centralize caller identity, enrollment, membership, key epochs, entry context, concurrency, and durable commit.
opportunities.diagnosis: Current code protects individual keys and files, but no component owns the complete distributed vault invariant or one durable generation transition.

evidence.claim: Every XPC connection is accepted and one exported handler owns privileged operations.
Enrollment, metadata, identity, key wrapping, and membership lifecycle share mutable file state without authenticated freshness.
Unshare performs an in-place multi-file rekey without a persisted transaction commit.
Repeated failures arise from dispersed ownership of identity and state transitions.

desiredInvariants: Every privileged helper request is authorized to the installed client identity.
Enrollment binds both device keys and the approved vault to one independently compared transcript.
Membership, key epoch, entries, and configuration belong to one authenticated committed generation.
Revocation rotates the key and rewraps only for remaining active devices.
Restart observes the old generation or resumes/commits the new generation, never a mixed-key state.

options.title: Strengthen local guards
options.summary: Add code-signing admission, AAD, locks, metadata authentication, containment checks, and a focused migration journal.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Direct guards cover observed paths but keep distributed ownership.

tradeoffs.assessment: Directly fixes observed paths but future callers can drift.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Re-run each finding regression and inventory every privileged sink.

tradeoffs.assessment: Checks and one mutex add little expected overhead.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark CLI add/get/list latency before and after.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new long-lived state is required.
A journal and mutex narrow races but several sources of truth remain.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Force termination through each migration step.

tradeoffs.assessment: Few new concepts; rejection and recovery telemetry are still needed.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review diagnostic output with CLI users.

tradeoffs.assessment: Most APIs remain stable, but AAD and metadata formats still need conversion.

residualRisks: File-provider lost updates remain difficult to resolve.

workPackages: Patch observed controls and add regression tests.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert focused guards while retaining reader compatibility.

options.title: Versioned transaction layer
options.summary: Commit authenticated immutable vault generations through one serialized transaction engine.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Centralizes the violated invariants while retaining direct caller-auth and migration fixes.

tradeoffs.assessment: One owner enforces caller, transcript, membership, context, revision, and commit invariants.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run unauthorized caller, race, replay, and revocation suites.

tradeoffs.assessment: Serialized commits and staging add I/O and queue latency.
Streaming rekey can avoid retaining all vault plaintext currently used by unshare.
Old-or-new generation commit and resume state replace in-place partial migration.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Force-kill every transaction phase and verify restart.

tradeoffs.assessment: Transaction IDs and phases support honest doctor/status/resume UX.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise recovery diagnostics with injected failures.

tradeoffs.assessment: A reader-first v3 schema and dual-generation rollout are required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run mixed-version device and rollback matrix.

residualRisks: All authorized endpoints can expose plaintext while active.

workPackages: Migrate lifecycle verbs and CLI diagnostics.
acceptanceCriteria: Crash at any phase yields a complete recoverable generation.
migrationNotes: Ship reader one release before writer.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Keep prior root generation and v3 reader compatibility.

options.title: Append-only signed operation log
options.summary: Represent device changes as signed mergeable operations and materialize a vault view.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Adds attribution and conflict semantics but creates a more complex distributed protocol.

tradeoffs.assessment: Signed operations provide attribution and explicit ordering, but fork/compaction rules become security-critical.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Model and test forks, replay, tombstones, epoch rotation, and malicious writers.

tradeoffs.assessment: Validation and compaction grow with log history.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark replay/checkpoint/steady-state sync at target histories.

tradeoffs.assessment: Materialized indexes and checkpoints add retained state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure index size and peak replay RSS.

tradeoffs.assessment: Explicit conflicts help, while forks and compaction introduce new failure modes.
Support must inspect, compact, and repair logs and forks.
All devices must transition to a versioned operation protocol with difficult downgrade.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise staged mixed-client rollout and rollback.

residualRisks: Consensus, fork, and compaction errors can replace current last-writer-wins failures.
Caller authentication and entry context still need tactical fixes.

workPackages: Specify operation protocol and security model before implementation.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Checkpoint export to a stable file generation before downgrade.

opportunities.recommendation: Choose versioned transactions unless offline multi-writer collaboration is a non-negotiable product requirement.

openQuestions: What recovery policy applies if every Secure Enclave identity is lost?
Which file providers preserve the required commit semantics?
What size and rekey-latency limits define release readiness?
